name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
blurb: Poached chicken, stock rice, ginger and chilli on the side.
condimentNote: Chilli, ginger and dark soy all come in saucers — just don't take them.

name: Roasted Chicken Rice
blurb: Roast chicken over stock rice, crisper skin than the poached.
condimentNote: Sauces on the side.

name: Bak Kut Teh
blurb: Peppery pork rib soup with garlic, you tiao and rice.
condimentNote: Dark soy + chilli dip is optional and separate.

name: Claypot Chicken Rice
blurb: Rice, chicken and lap cheong crisped in a clay pot.
seafoodNote: Most versions finish with oyster sauce, and some add dried scallop.
askFor: No oyster sauce — shellfish allergy. 不要蚝油，海鲜过敏。
condimentNote: Dark soy glaze, cooked in. Fine for her.

name: Salted Egg Chicken
blurb: Fried chicken tossed in salted duck egg yolk and curry leaf.
condimentNote: Salted egg and curry leaf — none of her four.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
blurb: Diced chicken, dried chilli, peanuts, Sichuan pepper.
condimentNote: Soy in the wok, not on the plate. Fine.

name: Sweet & Sour Pork
blurb: Battered pork, pineapple, capsicum in a red sauce.
condimentNote: The ketchup is cooked into a glaze, not squeezed on top.

name: Mapo Tofu
blurb: Silken tofu and minced pork in numbing bean paste.
seafoodNote: Some kitchens add dried shrimp or XO to the base.
askFor: No dried shrimp or XO sauce — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Doubanjiang is fermented bean, not soy sauce. Should be fine for her.

name: Beef Hor Fun
blurb: Flat rice noodles, beef, egg gravy, wok breath.
seafoodNote: The gravy is almost always built on oyster sauce.
askFor: No oyster sauce — shellfish allergy. This one is often refused; have a backup.
condimentNote: Gravy is cooked, nothing added at the table.

name: Wanton Mee
blurb: Springy egg noodles, char siu, dumplings, chilli sauce.
seafoodNote: Many wanton fillings mix prawn into the pork.
askFor: Pork-only wanton, no prawn — shellfish allergy. Some stalls can't split it.
condimentNote: Tossed in the kitchen. Ask for less chilli if she wants.

name: Bak Chor Mee
blurb: Minced pork noodles with vinegar, chilli and liver.
seafoodNote: Classic versions use fried sole fish (ti poh) in the sauce and stock.
askFor: No ti poh, no fish — allergy. Soup version is riskier than dry.
condimentNote: Vinegar and chilli go in at the stall — ask for less vinegar if she prefers.

name: Char Siew Rice
blurb: Barbecued pork over rice with blanched greens.
seafoodNote: The greens are usually dressed with oyster sauce.
askFor: Plain greens, no oyster sauce — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Glaze is on the meat, cooked in.

name: Roast Duck Rice
blurb: Roast or braised duck, rice, dark braising liquid.
condimentNote: Braise liquid, not a condiment.

name: Braised Duck Kway Chap
blurb: Braised duck, egg, tofu and broad rice sheets.
condimentNote: Everything is braised, nothing added after.

name: Chicken Cutlet Rice
blurb: Breaded fried chicken over rice, no fuss.
condimentNote: Sauce comes on the side or can be left off.

name: Sliced Fish Bee Hoon
blurb: Milky fish soup with rice vermicelli.
seafoodNote: It's a fish soup.

name: Hokkien Mee
blurb: Noodles braised in prawn stock with squid and lard.
seafoodNote: Prawn stock base, prawns and squid throughout.

name: Char Kway Teow
blurb: Wok-fried flat noodles with cockles, lap cheong and lard.
seafoodNote: Cockles, and dried shrimp in the chilli paste.

name: Yong Tau Foo
blurb: Pick-your-own stuffed tofu and vegetables in soup.
seafoodNote: The stuffing is fish paste and the broth is anchovy-based.

name: Fishball Noodles
blurb: Noodles with fishballs and fishcake.
seafoodNote: Fish, throughout.

name: Nasi Lemak
blurb: Coconut rice, fried chicken, egg, cucumber, sambal.
seafoodNote: Sambal is made with belacan (shrimp paste), and ikan bilis is anchovy.
askFor: No sambal and no ikan bilis — shellfish and fish allergy.
condimentNote: Without the sambal it's a clean plate — which suits her anyway.

name: Ayam Penyet
blurb: Smashed fried chicken, rice, tofu, tempeh, sambal.
seafoodNote: The sambal is belacan-based.
askFor: No sambal — shrimp paste allergy. Chicken and sides are fine.
condimentNote: Sambal arrives on the side of the plate.

name: Ayam Goreng Berempah
blurb: Spice-crusted fried chicken with rice.
seafoodNote: Served with sambal; some spice rubs include belacan.
askFor: No sambal, and check the marinade has no belacan.
condimentNote: Sambal is separate.

name: Soto Ayam
blurb: Turmeric chicken soup with rice cakes and bergedil.
condimentNote: Sambal and lime on the side.

name: Mee Rebus
blurb: Yellow noodles in thick sweet potato gravy.
seafoodNote: The gravy is usually built with dried shrimp or prawn stock.
askFor: Ask what's in the gravy — most stalls use dried shrimp. Often not worth the risk.
condimentNote: Sweet potato gravy — none of her four.

name: Beef Rendang with Rice
blurb: Slow-braised beef in dry coconut spice paste.
seafoodNote: A minority of rempah recipes include belacan.
askFor: Any belacan in the rendang? Shrimp allergy.
condimentNote: Coconut and rempah, no soy or vinegar.

name: Sup Kambing
blurb: Peppery mutton soup with bread to dunk.
condimentNote: Nothing added — a rare fully clean pick for her.

name: Nasi Padang
blurb: Point at a spread — beef, chicken, egg, vegetables.
seafoodNote: Several dishes on the counter use belacan or dried shrimp; the sambal always does.
askFor: You choose plate by plate — skip the sambal and anything with visible shrimp paste.
condimentNote: You control what goes on the plate.

name: Mee Goreng
blurb: Fried yellow noodles, sweet, spicy, wet.
seafoodNote: Usually contains prawn or squid, and the chilli paste uses belacan.
askFor: Often unavoidable — most stalls won't cook a separate batch.
condimentNote: Cooked in the wok. Nothing squeezed on at the table.

name: Nasi Goreng
blurb: Fried rice with egg, chicken and sweet dark soy.
seafoodNote: Terasi (shrimp paste) is standard in the seasoning; prawns are common.
askFor: No terasi, no prawns — shrimp allergy.
condimentNote: Kecap manis goes in during cooking.

name: Gado Gado
blurb: Blanched vegetables, tofu, egg, peanut sauce.
seafoodNote: Some peanut sauces are cut with shrimp paste.
askFor: Any belacan in the peanut sauce?
condimentNote: Peanut sauce — not one of her four.

name: Chicken Satay
blurb: Charcoal skewers with peanut sauce, ketupat, onion.
condimentNote: Peanut sauce, and it's a dip you control.

name: Sup Tulang Merah
blurb: Mutton bones in a red sauce, eaten with bread.
condimentNote: Cooked tomato-chilli sauce — messy but not a table condiment.

name: Chicken Biryani
blurb: Spiced long-grain rice with chicken, raita on the side.
condimentNote: Raita, achar and gravy all come separately.

name: Mutton Biryani
blurb: The same, with slow-cooked mutton.
condimentNote: Sides are separate.

name: Butter Chicken with Naan
blurb: Tomato-cream chicken curry, naan to mop it.
condimentNote: Tomato and cream, no condiments involved.

name: Tandoori Chicken
blurb: Yoghurt-marinated chicken straight off the clay oven.
condimentNote: Mint chutney comes on the side. The chicken itself is dry-cooked.

name: Chicken 65
blurb: Crisp, chilli-fried boneless chicken.
condimentNote: Eaten as-is.

name: Roti Prata with Curry
blurb: Flaky griddled flatbread, curry to dip.
condimentNote: The curry is a dip, not poured on — take dhal or chicken curry, not fish.

name: Murtabak
blurb: Prata stuffed with spiced minced mutton or chicken and egg.
condimentNote: Curry sauce on the side.

name: Thosai with Sambar
blurb: Fermented rice crepe with lentil stew and chutneys.
condimentNote: Sambar and chutney are dips — the thosai is plain.

name: Briyani Ayam Madu
blurb: Honey-glazed chicken over briyani rice.
condimentNote: Glaze is on the chicken; sides separate.

name: Palak Paneer with Rice
blurb: Spinach curry with cubes of fresh cheese.
condimentNote: Spinach and cream base.

name: Mutton Curry with Chapati
blurb: Dark peppery mutton curry, thin wholemeal bread.
condimentNote: A curry, not a condiment.

name: Roti John
blurb: Split baguette griddled with egg and minced meat.
condimentNote: Comes slathered in mayo and chilli sauce — ask for it plain.

name: Pad Krapow Gai
blurb: Chilli-basil minced chicken over rice with a fried egg.
seafoodNote: Built on fish sauce, and usually oyster sauce too.
askFor: No fish sauce, no oyster sauce — this changes the dish and many kitchens will say no.
condimentNote: Wok sauce, nothing added on top.

name: Green Curry Chicken
blurb: Coconut green curry with chicken and aubergine.
seafoodNote: Green curry paste contains shrimp paste, and fish sauce is added on top.

name: Pad Thai
blurb: Sweet-sour fried rice noodles with peanuts.
seafoodNote: Dried shrimp in the noodles, fish sauce and tamarind in the sauce.

name: Thai Grilled Chicken (Gai Yang)
blurb: Charcoal-grilled marinated chicken with sticky rice.
seafoodNote: The marinade is fish-sauce based.
askFor: Fish sauce in the marinade? It nearly always is.
condimentNote: Dipping sauce comes separately; the chicken is grilled dry.

name: Mango Sticky Rice
blurb: Coconut sticky rice with ripe mango. Yes, as dinner.
condimentNote: Nothing to skip.

name: Pho Bo
blurb: Beef broth, flat rice noodles, herbs, brisket.
seafoodNote: The broth is seasoned with fish sauce at almost every shop.
askFor: Fish sauce in the broth? Usually yes — worth asking before you sit.
condimentNote: Hoisin and sriracha come on the side; the broth itself is clean-tasting.

name: Banh Mi
blurb: Baguette with pork, pâté, pickles and coriander.
seafoodNote: Fish sauce in the pickle liquid and the meat marinade.
askFor: No fish sauce, no mayo.
condimentNote: Mayo and pâté are spread on the bread. Ask for no mayo.

name: Com Tam (Broken Rice)
blurb: Grilled pork chop over broken rice with egg.
seafoodNote: Nuoc cham dipping sauce is fish sauce, and the marinade often is too.
askFor: Hold the nuoc cham; ask about the marinade.
condimentNote: The dipping sauce is served separately.

name: Korean Fried Chicken
blurb: Double-fried chicken, soy-garlic or gochujang glaze.
condimentNote: Take the gochujang glaze, not the soy-garlic one.

name: Samgyeopsal
blurb: Grill your own pork belly with lettuce and banchan.
seafoodNote: Banchan often includes fermented seafood; some ssamjang has anchovy.
askFor: Skip the seafood banchan and the ssamjang — the pork itself is clean.
condimentNote: Every sauce is on the table, not on the meat.

name: Bibimbap
blurb: Rice bowl with vegetables, beef and a fried egg.
condimentNote: Gochujang comes on the side and isn't on her list anyway.

name: Budae Jjigae
blurb: Army stew — spam, sausage, ramyeon, kimchi.
seafoodNote: The broth base is usually anchovy stock, and fish cake is standard.
askFor: Anchovy stock is near-universal here.
condimentNote: Gochujang broth — none of her four.

name: Tteokbokki
blurb: Chewy rice cakes in sweet chilli sauce.
seafoodNote: Anchovy-kelp broth plus fish cake.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry
blurb: Panko chicken cutlet, Japanese curry, rice.
condimentNote: Japanese curry roux, not a condiment. The katsu is breaded and dry.

name: Chicken Karaage Don
blurb: Fried chicken over rice.
condimentNote: Comes with Japanese mayo — ask for it without.

name: Yakitori Set
blurb: Charcoal chicken skewers, rice, pickles.
seafoodNote: Some tare glazes are built on a dashi base.
askFor: Order shio (salt) instead of tare — grilled plain, no dashi.
condimentNote: Shio version is completely dry.

name: Gyudon
blurb: Simmered beef and onion over rice.
seafoodNote: The simmering liquid is dashi — bonito fish stock.
askFor: Dashi is structural here. Not really removable.
condimentNote: Simmered in the sauce, not dressed.

name: Tonkotsu Ramen
blurb: Pork bone broth, chashu, ajitama, thin noodles.
seafoodNote: Many shops blend niboshi (dried sardine) or dashi into the tare.
askFor: Is there any fish in the broth or tare? Pure tonkotsu shops exist — ask first.
condimentNote: Pork broth, not a sauce.

name: Sushi / Chirashi
blurb: Raw fish over rice.
seafoodNote: Obviously.

name: Udon in Broth
blurb: Thick wheat noodles in a clear soup.
seafoodNote: The broth is dashi — bonito and kombu.

name: Pepper Lunch Beef Pepper Rice
blurb: Raw beef, rice, corn and butter on a 260°C iron plate — you cook it yourself. Chicken and Hamburg versions too.
condimentNote: Honey Brown and Garlic Soy come in bottles on the table — nothing is poured on unless you do it.

name: Mala Xiang Guo
blurb: Pick your own ingredients by weight, wok-tossed in numbing chilli oil. Choose your spice level.
seafoodNote: You control the basket, but the wok and oil are shared with everyone else's prawns and squid — and some shop-made mala bases include dried shrimp.
askFor: Fresh wok and clean oil, no seafood — shellfish allergy. At a busy stall assume the oil is shared; the risk is real even with a clean basket.
condimentNote: Chilli and Sichuan pepper, none of her four. Skip the black vinegar if they offer it.

name: Economic Rice (Cai Fan)
blurb: Point at two or three dishes over rice. The cheapest honest dinner in Singapore.
seafoodNote: Seafood dishes share the counter, and most vegetable dishes are finished with oyster sauce.
askFor: You choose the plate — skip anything seafood, and ask whether the veg has oyster sauce.
condimentNote: You control exactly what lands on the plate.

name: Herbal Chicken Soup
blurb: Chicken simmered with wolfberry, red date and angelica root.
condimentNote: Nothing added.

name: ABC Soup with Rice
blurb: Pork rib, potato, carrot and tomato soup. Plain and good.
condimentNote: Nothing added.

name: Lotus Root & Pork Rib Soup
blurb: Long-simmered soup, faintly sweet from the root.
seafoodNote: Dried cuttlefish or dried scallop is a common depth ingredient.
askFor: Any dried cuttlefish or scallop in the soup?
condimentNote: Nothing added.

name: Marmite Chicken
blurb: Fried chicken in a dark, sweet-savoury yeast glaze.
condimentNote: Glaze is cooked on.

name: Coffee Pork Ribs
blurb: Fried ribs in a sticky coffee caramel.
condimentNote: Cooked glaze, nothing added after.

name: Black Pepper Beef
blurb: Beef strips, onion and capsicum in coarse black pepper.
seafoodNote: Oyster sauce is the usual base for the pepper gravy.
askFor: No oyster sauce — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Wok sauce.

name: Hotplate Tofu
blurb: Egg tofu with minced pork and gravy on a sizzling plate.
seafoodNote: Prawns are usually in it, and the gravy is oyster-sauce based.
askFor: No prawns, no oyster sauce — many kitchens will refuse.
condimentNote: Gravy is cooked.

name: French Bean with Minced Pork
blurb: Blistered beans wok-tossed with pork and garlic.
seafoodNote: Dried shrimp (hae bee) is the classic addition.
askFor: No dried shrimp — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Wok-tossed, nothing added.

name: Sambal Kangkong
blurb: Water spinach in chilli paste.
seafoodNote: The sambal is belacan — shrimp paste is what makes it sambal.

name: Har Cheong Gai
blurb: Chicken wings fried in fermented prawn paste batter.
seafoodNote: Prawn paste is the batter.

name: Xiao Long Bao
blurb: Soup dumplings, pork and hot broth in a thin skin.
condimentNote: Vinegar and ginger come in a dish — she just won't take it.

name: Char Siew Bao
blurb: Steamed buns filled with sweet barbecued pork.
condimentNote: Nothing on the side.

name: Siew Mai & Har Gow
blurb: The two dim sum everyone orders first.
seafoodNote: Har gow is prawn, and siew mai is topped with prawn or roe.

name: Chee Cheong Fun
blurb: Silky steamed rice rolls in sweet and sesame sauce.
seafoodNote: Many stalls fold dried shrimp into the rolls or the sauce.
askFor: No dried shrimp — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Sauce is poured in the kitchen.

name: Fried Carrot Cake
blurb: Cubes of radish cake fried with egg and preserved radish.
seafoodNote: Dried shrimp is standard in the white version at most stalls.
askFor: No dried shrimp — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Cooked in the wok.

name: Oyster Omelette
blurb: Egg, starch and oysters, crisp at the edges.
seafoodNote: Oysters.

name: Popiah
blurb: Soft rolls of stewed turnip, egg and peanut.
seafoodNote: Dried shrimp is in the turnip filling almost everywhere.
askFor: No dried shrimp in the filling — shellfish allergy.
condimentNote: Sweet sauce is spread inside — ask for light.

name: Yang Chow Fried Rice
blurb: Egg fried rice with char siew and prawns.
seafoodNote: Prawns are a defining ingredient.

name: Olive Fried Rice
blurb: Fried rice with preserved olive leaf, minced pork and long bean.
condimentNote: Cooked in the wok.

name: Beef La Mian
blurb: Hand-pulled noodles in clear beef broth with radish.
condimentNote: Chilli oil on the side.

name: Hainanese Pork Chop
blurb: Cracker-crumbed pork with peas and a tangy brown sauce.
condimentNote: Sauce is cooked and poured in the kitchen.

name: Braised Pork Belly Rice
blurb: Lu rou fan — soy-braised pork over rice with pickled greens.
condimentNote: Braised, not dressed.

name: Chicken Macaroni Soup
blurb: Clear soup, macaroni, shredded chicken. Deliberately plain.
condimentNote: Nothing added.

name: Steamboat
blurb: Cook it yourself at the table in a shared pot.
seafoodNote: The pot is shared and seafood goes in it. For an allergy, a shared broth is the risk, not the basket.
askFor: Split pot, and nothing seafood on your side — still not zero risk.
condimentNote: Dipping sauces are self-serve.

name: Curry Chicken Noodles
blurb: Coconut curry broth, yellow noodles, chicken and puffs.
seafoodNote: Some curry bases are built with dried shrimp, and cockles get added at a few stalls.
askFor: No cockles, and check the curry base for dried shrimp.
condimentNote: Broth, not a condiment.

name: Bulgogi with Rice
blurb: Sweet marinated beef, grilled and served over rice.
condimentNote: Marinade is cooked in.

name: Kimchi Jjigae
blurb: Sour kimchi stew with pork belly and tofu.
seafoodNote: Kimchi is nearly always fermented with jeotgal — shrimp or anchovy — and the stock is often anchovy.
askFor: This one is hard to make safe. Vegan kimchi exists but is rare in restaurants.
condimentNote: Stew.

name: Doenjang Jjigae
blurb: Soybean paste stew with tofu, courgette and pork.
seafoodNote: The stock is usually anchovy-and-kelp.
askFor: Anchovy stock in the base? Most places, yes.
condimentNote: Stew.

name: Samgyetang
blurb: Whole young chicken stuffed with rice and ginseng in clear broth.
condimentNote: Salt and pepper on the side, nothing else.

name: Dakgalbi
blurb: Chicken, cabbage and rice cake stir-fried in gochujang at the table.
seafoodNote: Some marinades use anchovy stock or seafood extract for depth.
askFor: Any seafood stock in the sauce?
condimentNote: Gochujang, not on her list.

name: Jjajangmyeon
blurb: Thick noodles in black bean sauce with pork and onion.
seafoodNote: Squid is a common addition and some sauces are seafood-stocked.
askFor: Pork only, no squid — usually easy.
condimentNote: Sauce is cooked and poured in the kitchen.

name: Kimbap
blurb: Seaweed rice rolls with egg, pickle, carrot and meat.
seafoodNote: Crab stick and tuna are the two most common fillings.
askFor: Beef or vegetable kimbap only — no crab stick, no tuna.
condimentNote: Nothing on the side.

name: Korean Corn Dog
blurb: Battered sausage and cheese, rolled in sugar.
condimentNote: It arrives striped with ketchup and mustard — ask for it bare.

name: Chicken Teriyaki Don
blurb: Glazed grilled chicken over rice.
condimentNote: Glaze is brushed on during grilling.

name: Japanese Curry Rice
blurb: Thick mild curry over rice, usually with a cutlet.
condimentNote: Curry roux, not a condiment.

name: Omurice
blurb: Omelette over fried rice.
condimentNote: Ketchup is both in the rice and squeezed across the top — this one is genuinely out.

name: Oyakodon
blurb: Chicken and egg simmered together over rice.
seafoodNote: The simmering liquid is dashi — bonito stock.
askFor: Dashi is structural. Not removable.
condimentNote: Simmered.

name: Tonkatsu Set
blurb: Panko pork cutlet, shredded cabbage, rice and pickles.
seafoodNote: Tonkatsu sauce is Worcestershire-based, which means anchovy.
askFor: Cutlet with salt or ponzu instead of tonkatsu sauce — the pork itself is clean.
condimentNote: Sauce is poured by you, at the table.

name: Chicken Nanban
blurb: Fried chicken in sweet vinegar with tartar sauce.
condimentNote: Tartar is mayonnaise, and it's ladled over the chicken.

name: Wagyu Beef Don
blurb: Seared beef over rice with onsen egg.
seafoodNote: The tare is usually dashi-based.
askFor: Any dashi in the sauce? Ask for salt-seasoned if they offer it.
condimentNote: Sauce is cooked in.

name: Shabu Shabu
blurb: Swish thin slices through hot broth at your table.
seafoodNote: The kombu-dashi broth and the shared pot both carry seafood.

name: Soba
blurb: Buckwheat noodles, hot or cold, with dipping broth.
seafoodNote: Tsuyu is dashi — bonito and kombu.

name: Okonomiyaki
blurb: Savoury cabbage pancake with sauce and bonito.
seafoodNote: Bonito flakes on top, dashi in the batter, squid in most versions.

name: Khao Man Gai
blurb: Thai chicken rice with a fermented soybean and ginger sauce.
condimentNote: Sauce arrives in its own dish.

name: Moo Ping with Sticky Rice
blurb: Charcoal pork skewers, coconut-marinated, with sticky rice.
seafoodNote: Fish sauce is in the marinade.
askFor: Fish sauce in the marinade? Almost always yes.
condimentNote: Nothing added after grilling.

name: Larb Gai
blurb: Minced chicken with lime, chilli, mint and toasted rice.
seafoodNote: Fish sauce is the salt in this dish.
askFor: Soy instead of fish sauce — some kitchens will, most won't.
condimentNote: Dressed in the kitchen.

name: Tom Kha Gai
blurb: Coconut galangal chicken soup, sour and creamy.
seafoodNote: Fish sauce is standard seasoning.
askFor: No fish sauce — fish allergy.
condimentNote: Soup.

name: Pandan Chicken
blurb: Marinated chicken wrapped in pandan leaf and fried.
seafoodNote: Oyster and fish sauce are both usual in the marinade.
askFor: No oyster sauce, no fish sauce in the marinade.
condimentNote: Nothing on the side.

name: Bun Bo Hue
blurb: Spicy lemongrass beef noodle soup from central Vietnam.
seafoodNote: Shrimp paste is what gives the broth its character.

name: Bun Thit Nuong
blurb: Grilled pork over cold vermicelli with herbs and peanuts.
seafoodNote: Nuoc cham — fish sauce — is poured over the whole bowl.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
blurb: Grilled chicken in a spiced tomato cream sauce.
condimentNote: A cooked curry, not a condiment.

name: Rogan Josh
blurb: Kashmiri lamb curry, deep red from chilli, not heat.
condimentNote: Curry.

name: Dal Makhani with Naan
blurb: Black lentils slow-cooked overnight with butter and cream.
condimentNote: Nothing on the side.

name: Chana Masala
blurb: Chickpeas in a tangy onion-tomato masala.
condimentNote: Curry.

name: Paneer Tikka
blurb: Charred marinated cheese and peppers off the tandoor.
condimentNote: Mint chutney in a bowl on the side.

name: Mutton Keema with Naan
blurb: Spiced minced mutton with peas.
condimentNote: Cooked, nothing added.

name: Chicken Chettinad
blurb: Peppery Tamil chicken curry, dark with roasted spice.
condimentNote: Curry.

name: Kothu Parotta
blurb: Parotta shredded on the griddle with egg, meat and curry.
condimentNote: Cooked together on the griddle.

name: Idli with Sambar
blurb: Steamed rice cakes with lentil stew and chutney.
condimentNote: Sambar and chutney are dips.

name: Appam with Coconut Milk
blurb: Lacy fermented rice pancakes with sweet coconut milk.
condimentNote: Nothing to leave off.

name: Indian Rojak
blurb: Fried fritters dunked in a thick sweet chilli sauce.
seafoodNote: Prawn fritters and cuttlefish are on the tray, and the sauce is shrimp-thickened.

name: Mee Soto
blurb: Yellow noodles in spiced chicken broth with shredded chicken.
condimentNote: Sambal on the side.

name: Lontong
blurb: Compressed rice cakes in coconut vegetable stew.
seafoodNote: Sayur lodeh is usually built with dried shrimp, and serunding is often anchovy.
askFor: Dried shrimp in the lodeh? Nearly always.
condimentNote: Stew, poured in the kitchen.

name: Kurma Chicken with Rice
blurb: Mild coconut and cashew curry, gently spiced.
condimentNote: Curry.

name: Ayam Masak Merah
blurb: Fried chicken simmered in a sweet tomato chilli gravy.
seafoodNote: Some cooks build the chilli base on belacan.
askFor: Belacan in the gravy?
condimentNote: Cooked gravy.

name: Tahu Goreng
blurb: Fried tofu with cucumber and thick peanut sauce.
seafoodNote: Some peanut sauces are seasoned with shrimp paste.
askFor: Belacan in the peanut sauce?
condimentNote: Sauce is poured over.

name: Bakso
blurb: Beef meatball soup with noodles and fried wonton.
condimentNote: Chilli and sweet soy are self-serve at the table.

name: Nasi Ambeng
blurb: A shared tray of rice, chicken, beef, vegetables and serunding.
seafoodNote: Serunding and sambal on the tray usually contain anchovy or dried shrimp.
askFor: Skip the serunding and sambal — the rest of the tray is fine.
condimentNote: Everything is separate on the tray.

name: Fish & Chips
blurb: Battered fish, fries, tartar.
seafoodNote: Fish.

name: Chicken Parmigiana
blurb: Crumbed chicken under tomato and melted mozzarella.
condimentNote: Baked together, nothing added.

name: Mac & Cheese
blurb: Baked pasta in a thick cheese sauce.
condimentNote: Nothing to leave off.

name: Grilled Lamb Chops
blurb: Chops with mint, potatoes and greens.
condimentNote: Sauce comes on the side.

name: Caesar Salad
blurb: Cos lettuce, parmesan, croutons, thick dressing.
seafoodNote: Caesar dressing is built on anchovy.
askFor: There's anchovy in the dressing — ask, most kitchens won't make it without.
condimentNote: The dressing is mayonnaise-based and tossed through.

name: Club Sandwich
blurb: Triple-decker with chicken, egg, bacon and lettuce.
condimentNote: Mayo is spread on every layer — ask for it dry or skip.

name: Full English Breakfast
blurb: Eggs, sausage, bacon, beans, mushroom, toast. At dinner, why not.
condimentNote: Ketchup and brown sauce come in bottles on the table.

name: Buffalo Chicken Wings
blurb: Fried wings tossed in hot sauce.
condimentNote: The blue cheese or ranch dip is a separate pot.

name: Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs poached in spiced tomato and pepper, bread to dip.
condimentNote: Nothing added.

name: Lamb Kabsa
blurb: Spiced rice baked with lamb, tomato and dried lime.
condimentNote: Sauces come in bowls.

name: Manakish Za'atar
blurb: Flatbread baked with thyme, sesame and olive oil.
condimentNote: Nothing on it but herbs and oil.

name: Chicken Gyro
blurb: Shaved chicken, tomato, onion and tzatziki in pita.
condimentNote: Tzatziki is yoghurt and cucumber — not on her list, and it can be left out.

name: Beef Burrito
blurb: Rice, beans, beef and salsa rolled in a flour tortilla.
condimentNote: Salsa and sour cream, not mayo or ketchup. You pick the fillings.

name: Chicken Quesadilla
blurb: Griddled tortilla folded over chicken and melted cheese.
condimentNote: Dips on the side.

name: Loaded Nachos
blurb: Corn chips under cheese, beans, jalapeño and beef.
condimentNote: Sour cream and guacamole in separate pots.

name: Babi Pongteh
blurb: Pork braised with fermented soy bean and mushroom.
condimentNote: Slow-braised in taucheo.

name: Itek Tim
blurb: Salted vegetable and duck soup, sour and savoury.
condimentNote: Nothing added.

name: Ayam Buah Keluak
blurb: Chicken with black nuts in a deep rempah gravy.
seafoodNote: Most rempah recipes include belacan.
askFor: Belacan in the rempah? Usually yes.
condimentNote: Rempah and black nut — none of her four.

name: Chicken Chop
blurb: Grilled chicken thigh, fries, coleslaw, black pepper sauce.
condimentNote: Sauce on the side, coleslaw is mayo — swap it for salad.

name: Ribeye Steak
blurb: Steak, fries, whatever green they give you.
condimentNote: Sauces come separately.

name: Roast Chicken & Sides
blurb: Half a roast chicken with potatoes and greens.
condimentNote: Gravy on the side.

name: Carbonara
blurb: Egg, pecorino, guanciale, black pepper. No cream.
condimentNote: Nothing to skip.

name: Bolognese
blurb: Slow beef and tomato ragù over pasta.
condimentNote: Slow tomato ragù, closer to a braise than a sauce.

name: Aglio Olio
blurb: Garlic, chilli and olive oil pasta.
seafoodNote: Many kitchens melt anchovy into the oil for depth.
askFor: No anchovy in the oil — fish allergy.
condimentNote: Just oil and garlic.

name: Margherita Pizza
blurb: Tomato, mozzarella, basil.
condimentNote: Nothing on the side.

name: Beef Burger
blurb: Patty, cheese, bun, fries.
condimentNote: Ketchup and mayo are spread inside — order it dry, cheese only.

name: Chicken Shawarma Plate
blurb: Shaved chicken, rice or bread, salad, garlic toum.
condimentNote: Toum and chilli come on the side.

name: Lamb Mandi
blurb: Slow-smoked lamb over spiced long-grain rice.
condimentNote: Sauces come in bowls, not on the rice.

name: Falafel Wrap
blurb: Chickpea fritters, salad, tahini in flatbread.
condimentNote: Tahini is sesame. Ask for it light if she wants.

name: Mixed Grill Platter
blurb: Lamb, chicken and kofta skewers with rice and salad.
condimentNote: Everything's grilled dry; sauces on the side.
